Dylan — thanks for the ping. Quick run of ops feasibility:

Summary: The 250ms p95 for the committed baseline at 50k req/day in us-west is achievable but depends on 2 constraints: (1) whether Falkon will accept a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) vs. multi-tenant hosted, and (2) whether we can require a regional fallback policy that preserves availability over strict latency during overloads.

Requirements and caveats:
- Dedicated GPU pool (m5g-dedicated-3 or equivalent) or guaranteed capacity slices for the committed QPS. We can model throughput but tail latency depends on request size/sequence length.
- KV/prefix caching and continuous batching configuration must be enabled; recommend aggressive prefix cache for Falkon to reduce hot-starts.
- We will need 24/7 on-call coverage in first 90 days with a documented runbook and a monthly performance review (first 3 months weekly).
- Fallback behaviour: propose explicit fallback to a smaller model variant or regional redirect (us-east) when we detect sustained saturation. That should be in the SLA as an allowed remediation before credits.

Operational artifacts we will produce if approved:
1) Operational_Runbook_v1.xlsx (runbook + playbook + escalation matrix)
2) SLO measurement dashboard (hosted) with token-level traces shared to Falkon's monitoring project (view-only)

Open questions for product/engineering:
- Can product guarantee the required model variant fallback with automated routing?
- Any restrictions on committing to a numeric p95 for all input distributions? We should limit to standard request profile (<=1024 tokens).

Labeling: I'd recommend this be an SLA exception with a 6-month operational review clause. Happy to join a live technical call with Falkon.

-Monica
Director, Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: one-year p95 latency commitment for Falkon — legal/pricing considerations

Dylan / team — flagged a few contract-level considerations:

1) Credits and measurement window: We should limit credits such that they do not exceed X% of monthly bill and apply only after a 72-hour incident window during which we must demonstrate remediation. Recommend a capped credit schedule and a remediation-first clause.
2) Force majeure / capacity constraints: Add a clause that allows Redwood to use pre-agreed fallback policies (e.g., regional redirect, lower-quality model) without triggering credits provided customers are notified and we comply with runbook steps.
3) Scope of p95 guarantee: Must be scoped to specific model family, max prompt length (e.g., <=1024 tokens), and the committed baseline QPS. Anything outside should be excluded.
4) Termination and exit: Include an operational handoff and data retention terms for the dedicated pool.

If Sales wants to approve this exception, pricing will need to include a margin uplift and a playbook for capacity upgrades. I recommend we require an initial three-month dedicated capacity commit and a quarterly review to re-evaluate.

I can draft redline language for the SOW and SLA table. If Laura signs off on the exception framework, we can present to Falkon next week.

-Markus
Head of Legal Operations (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: one-year p95 latency commitment for Falkon — need ops/product + pricing sign-off

Thanks everyone for the quick responses and clear options. Executive decision: we will approve a one-year SLA exception for Falkon with these binding conditions:

- Commitment: 250ms p95 for agreed baseline (50k req/day) in us-west, scoped to model family A (v2) and <=1024 token requests.
- Operational prerequisites: Dedicated capacity for first 3 months, detailed runbook delivered and tested prior to go-live, 24/7 on-call coverage for first 90 days.
- Fallback clause: Allow automated regional redirect or model-variant fallback as remediation; credits only apply after documented remediation steps within 72 hours.
- Financial: This exception requires pricing uplift of 18% over list to cover reserved capacity and SRE support. Sales to confirm final pricing with Markus.
- Review: 6-month operational review and subjective SLA health gating future renewals.

Action items:
- Monica: produce Operational_Runbook_v1.xlsx and test playbook by 2027-03-30.
- Markus: send redlined SLA + SOW text to Falkon by 2027-03-26.
- Dylan: confirm pricing and send initial acceptance to Falkon; include the DocuSign link and attach the runbook once ready.

I approve this exception on the condition that all three action items are completed. Once Markus and Monica attach their artifacts we will finalize.

-Laura
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
